methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Uptool operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at an undisclosed stage. The addressable comp universe comprises one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the narrow peer set presents a material constraint on valuation methodology.

The Peer-Median approach is not applicable. Despite ten same-sector companies existing in Robotics & Manufacturing, filtering for matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier yields fewer than three datapoints in any filtered subset. Using an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given heterogeneity in robotics subsegments, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines. No triangulated valuation range can therefore be derived from the available comparable data.

The analysis underscores that Uptool's valuation—absent stage disclosure, financing history, and operational metrics—cannot be anchored to market multiples or peer benchmarks with confidence. A credible valuation would require either (1) disclosure of Uptool's stage and recent financing terms to enable peer filtering, (2) operational metrics (revenue, deployment scale, burn rate) to support DCF or revenue-multiple approaches, or (3) expansion of the comp set to adjacent subsectors (industrial automation, supply-chain robotics) with explicit justification for cross-segment comparison. The single public comparable offers limited direct reference without context on Uptool's business model maturity.
